summary: A border's width and colour now take keys like any other value, so a picture can grow a frame as it lands and a title's outline can change colour over a clip. Changing a keyed colour from the panel at a later moment now adds a key there, for shadows and glows as well as borders.
setup: Photonz Dev, release Next, no flag changed from its default. The walk is border-width-keys-walk.

try.do: Open a recording, pick it, click the plus on Effects and choose Border, then set the Border's Position to Inside.
With the playhead at 0:00, click Animate a property in Properties and pick Border width, then type 0 and press Return.
Move the playhead to 0:01, type 12 into Border width and press Return.
Put the playhead at half a second and read the value, the diamond and the frame.
Back at 0:00, pick Border color from Animate a property, move to 0:01 and paint the border a new colour from the panel.
Go to the start and press Space to play it.
On a title with no Border, pick Border width from Animate a property and key it from 0 to 6.

evaluate: Does the frame growing in round the recording over the first second read as the picture landing?
Are Border width and Border color the names you would look for, and is it clear they are not a line's own Stroke width?
When you paint a keyed border colour from the Effects list at a later moment, does it feel like it added a key, the way typing a number does?
Keying Border width up on a layer with no Border brings one in, inside the edge. Is that what you would expect, or should you have to add the Border first?
rough: A Border added from the Effects plus lands Outside, and a recording fills the whole frame, so the ring is drawn off the canvas and nothing shows until Position is set to Inside. The walk sets Inside for this reason: task a-border-added-to-a-picture-that-fills-the-frame.

The video mock groups Border width and Border color under Appearance; the app lists them under Effects because the Border now lives in the Effects list: task outline-leaves-appearance-and-an-effect-s-colour.
Offering Border width and Border color on every picture layer matches the mock's catalogue. A width key above 0 on a layer with no Border brings an Inside ring in.
A keyed colour flattens a gradient border to one colour while it plays.
Only the first Border in the list takes keys; a second ring keeps its own width and colour.
Animate a property now lists 14 values for a clip or a title, so Border color sits below the fold of the picker until you scroll or type in Find a property.
A border's Offset and Position still cannot take keys.
